author: ephron
imp: Open with a declarative thesis sentence that sounds like a confident, slightly absurd personal law — state it flat, as fact, not opinion.
Follow the thesis immediately with a concrete, domestic illustration that proves it, using specific nouns (dishwasher, silverware basket, pear-shaped candle) rather than abstract categories.
Build sentences in threes: establish a pattern with the first two clauses, then break or subvert it with the third — the third clause is where the joke or the wound lives.
Use short, blunt sentences as punctuation after longer ones. Let the short sentence land the point. Do not explain it afterward.
Repeat a key word or phrase within a paragraph to create a drumbeat effect, then twist the meaning on the final repetition ('The chicken is fine. The chicken is always fine.').
Confess the unflattering thing about yourself before the reader can think it — name your own ridiculousness directly and without softening, then keep moving.
Avoid adverbs; when intensification is needed, repeat the word or restructure the sentence so the verb or noun carries the force.
End paragraphs with a sentence that reframes everything above it — a small reversal, a resignation, or a rueful summary that widens the personal into the universal.
Anchor abstract emotional states to a single physical object or action; the object does the emotional work so the prose never has to announce a feeling directly.
Use parenthetical asides and subordinate clauses to perform the mind catching itself mid-thought — but keep them short enough that they feel like interruptions, not digressions.
When writing about time, compress years into a single image or gesture rather than narrating sequence; let one detail stand for the whole era.
Employ the second person ('you') sparingly and strategically to suddenly pull the reader into complicity with behavior the narrator has just confessed to.
Let lists do comic work: build a list of three or more items in which the final item is either bathetically small or wildly out of scale with the others.
Never resolve ambivalence — end on the acknowledgment of contradiction, not its solution, and frame that contradiction as the only honest available position.
Write the self as a character who is intelligent enough to see her own absurdity clearly and powerless to change it anyway; that gap between insight and behavior is the engine of every piece.
